highlights.text: A different life, if she hadn’t gone. Less wind, less rain. Perhaps none of the visions offered those who stand in the high, windy places of the world.
There are moments in some lives when it can truly be said that everything pivots and changes, when the branching paths show clearly, when one does make a choice.
He had been proud without vanity, wise without trivial wit, courageous without bravado. He was a shell, a husk, a blind, mute absence of all these things in a room without light.
In a way, Jehane thought—looking at her father, preparing to say goodbye—pursuing this vengeance, however belated, against Almalik of Cartada was the most obvious thing she had ever done.
The deeds of men, as footprints in the desert.

Things changed then. Things began to change everywhere.
Small, good things, it seemed, still happened in the world.
If someone doesn’t do it before either of us, he had said that night. Someone had.

I want this peninsula back. I want Esperaña great again, but I will not pretend that if we smash Al-Rassan and all it has built we are doing the will of any god I know.”
There was nothing he could think of to say. There were places into which words could not go. Not the words he knew.
